title: Match the day's approvals with the clearing file

blocks.text: A merchant group's acquirer gets the network's acknowledgement file every morning: one record per sale it presented the day before. Its operations team wants one report that says, for every record and every approval, what happened to it, so that each finding goes to whoever has to act.

`ClearingMatcher.match` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/ClearingMatcher.java` builds that report: one `Result` per clearing record, in the file's order, then one per approval that no record presented, in the journal's order. The kinds of finding are in `Kind`. Finish the three methods marked `TODO`; the comment on each says what it is for. About fifteen lines in total.
The tests use several terminals and compare whole lists of `Result`s.

cases.says: each record that finds its approval at the same amount is MATCHED, in the file's order
a clearing record with no approval in the journal is NOT_AUTHORIZED
an approval no record presented is reported as NOT_PRESENTED after the records
two terminals may use the same RRN, so the key is the terminal with the RRN
a record presented again after its approval was paired is a DUPLICATE_PRESENTMENT naming that approval
a record whose amount differs from its approval is AMOUNT_DIFFERS
approvals never presented are reported in the journal's order

origin.section: 19.5. Matching Puts Every Record in One Category, and Each Category Has an Owner

concepts: Matching on the terminal with the RRN puts every clearing record and every approval in exactly one category: matched, amount differs, duplicate presentment, not authorized or not presented.
